sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 'Tons' (p. 628): four tones corresponding to Chinese tones 1-4, first tone in two heights; 'quand les mots entrent en composition, ou même suivant leur simple position dans la phrase, ils changent facilement de ton'; dictionary preface adds that short vowels may lengthen in composition. 'accent' appears only as a French gloss in two dictionary entries.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. I 'Les sons et les mots' (pp. 285-288) gives vowels, vowel length (a, i, o short vs long), four tones matching the four Chinese tones (1st tone in an upper and lower register), aspiration, syllable structure (strictly CV monosyllables); a remark says tones need only be marked on words 'auxquels la voix doit donner une importance prédominante dans la phrase'. The word 'accent' does not occur anywhere in the 30 pages.
